item.title: [16★] Improved Digitization Bounds for U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory via Semiclassical Analysis
item.author: Di Fang, Yu Tong
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Di Fang, Yu Tong

arXiv ID: 2611.26720 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Simulating lattice gauge theories on a digital quantum computer or using tensor network methods requires a finite-dimensional approximation of the gauge field, a process often called digitization. Controlling the resulting error is essential for assessing the accuracy and resource requirements of these simulations. In this work, we derive a digitization error bound for low-lying eigenstates of the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian for pure U(1) gauge theory and translate it into a bound on time-evolution error. Compared with existing bounds, our result achieves exponentially improved dependence on the inverse lattice spacing 1/a1/a1/a and evolution time TTT, together with improved dependence on the inverse coupling 1/g1/g1/g. The key idea is to identify a small parameter in the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian and apply tools from semiclassical analysis. Specifically, we adapt Agmon's method to establish exponential decay of the error with the truncation threshold. These results sharpen estimates of the local Hilbert space dimension and qubit resources needed to simulate gauge theories near the continuum limit, at weak coupling, and over long times.

Di Fang, Yu Tong

item.title: [9★] Scheduling the quantum implementation of the Trotter decomposition for Hamiltonian simulation
item.author: Augustin Ho, Naoki Yamamoto
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Augustin Ho, Naoki Yamamoto

arXiv ID: 2611.26884 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

For the quantum computational task for Hamiltonian simulation, the arrangement in which sub-Hamiltonians appear in the Trotter decomposition may have a large influence on the precision, under a given circuit complexity. In this paper, we design several scheduling strategies by combining two methods; that is, the existing simultaneous diagonalization scheme leveraged in order to guarantee the performance in a relatively short circuit depth, with a method inspired from a Trotter-Suzuki decomposition of the second or the fourth order for a better accuracy. By conducting numerical simulations on various Hamiltonian instances, we confirm a systematic advantage over previous methods. Thus, our proposal may eliminate the need of dealing with several Hamiltonian-dependent scheduling strategies.

Augustin Ho, Naoki Yamamoto

item.title: [6★] Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
item.author: Sayantan Ganguly
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Sayantan Ganguly

arXiv ID: 2611.27300 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

An FqFq\mathbb{F}_q-linear [[n,k]]q[[n,k]]q[[n,k]]_q stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of F2nqF2nq\mathbb{F}_q^{2n} of dimension n−kn−kn-k, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a 333-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly 222, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over \F2\F2\F_2 a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for q≥3q≥3q\ge3 even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

Sayantan Ganguly

item.title: [6★] Certification of non-stabilizerness in multi-qubit systems via worst-case random access codes
item.author: Santiago Zamora
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Santiago Zamora

arXiv ID: 2611.26705 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Recent works have proposed semi-device-independent frameworks to certify non-stabilizerness, but the complexity of the stabilizer polytope makes these methods infeasible beyond a few qubits. In this work, we address this limitation by moving to partially characterized measurements in the context of worst-case random access codes. We first establish a simple condition, which we term the stabilizer pigeonhole criterion, that certifies non-stabilizerness in mmm-qubit pure states, and show how it can be applied to reduced states. As an application, we certify magic in WWW states of arbitrary size using only eight preparations and three single-qubit measurement settings. Motivated by recent work on the stabilizer marginal problem, we then construct prepare-and-measure correlations generated by global mmm-qubit quantum states for which every kkk-qubit marginal lies inside the stabilizer polytope, yet the combined correlations cannot be reproduced by any global stabilizer mixture. Finally, we derive analytical upper and lower bounds on the worst-case bias attainable with mixed stabilizer preparations in an mmm-qubit random access code with nnn Pauli measurements. For the complete set of 4m−14m−14^m-1 non-identity Pauli measurements, we show that the optimal quantum and mixed-stabilizer biases both scale as 2−3m/22−3m/22^{-3m/2}, and that their ratio is asymptotically bounded by a constant (≲1.85\lesssim 1.85), showing that in this setting, magic in the preparations alone yields at most a constant-factor advantage over stabilizer mixtures.

Santiago Zamora

item.title: [1★] Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
item.author: Yicheng Song, ..., Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Yicheng Song, ..., Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka

arXiv ID: 2611.26762 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.

Yicheng Song, ..., Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka

item.title: [1★] Efficient Tensor Decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like Potentials and Its Application to Probing Molecular Geometries Using a Quantum Computer
item.author: James Brown, ..., Robert Wodraszka, James Whitfield
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: James Brown, ..., Robert Wodraszka, James Whitfield

arXiv ID: 2611.26740 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We present an efficient canonical polyadic decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like potentials in real-space grid representations suited to quantum computing applications. By decomposing the matrix elements of Coulomb-like potentials into low-rank Cartesian components, we achieve O(N1/3)O(N^{1/3}) T-gate scaling per Coulomb term, where NN is the number of grid points (basis functions) per electron, while maintaining high accuracy. This opens a path to significantly reducing the number of basis functions (i.e., qubits) required compared to previous methods by utilizing improved representations of the Coulomb potential that converge faster with grid spacing. The decomposition is also valid for certain pseudopotentials, which can decrease the cost significantly compared to previous work. This efficient decomposition enables the application of block-encoding techniques at larger grid spacings than with previous decompositions, and can therefore be used for algorithms that do not require high energy accuracy. We apply this decomposed Coulomb potential to hydrogen atom energy levels, the helium ground-state energy, and the Hartree-Fock potential energy curve of LiH, and show that modest basis sizes achieve semi-quantitative to quantitative accuracy. As an example of where these faster-converging Coulomb representations can be used on a quantum computer, we discuss their application to probing low-energy molecular geometries, and we estimate the resulting reduction in the cost of real-time evolution.

James Brown, ..., Robert Wodraszka, James Whitfield

item.title: [0★] Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
item.author: Tianchun Zhou
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Tianchun Zhou

arXiv ID: 2611.27295 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emphwithout receiving any input from traditional analytical methods. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text-- supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text-- hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emphactive supersymmetrization transformations, \emphmomentum operator maps as well as plain and \emphhigher-order spin matrix maps. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

Tianchun Zhou

item.title: [0★] Pulse-tube-vibration induced Larmor frequency jitter in anisotropic Kramers spins
item.author: R. Shaik, ..., S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: R. Shaik, ..., S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan

arXiv ID: 2611.27267 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate the role of pulse-tube mechanical vibrations towards spin frequency noise in a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator. Our system comprises of a low mode-volume superconducting resonator coupled to 50 ppm Er3+:CaWO4\text{Er}^{3+}:\text{CaWO}_4 spins with highly anisotropic g-factors. By measuring single-shot spin echoes using narrow-bandwidth three-pulse sequences, we directly observe a vibration induced stochastic signal resulting from the spin's Larmor frequency moving into and out of the detection bandwidth. The sensitivity to these vibrations is substantially suppressed when a) the external magnetic field is aligned along the symmetry c-axis and b) spin temperature is modestly increased to 60~mK. We also benchmark the system as a quantum sensor for angular fluctuations, extracting a noise floor of 350 nanodegrees.

R. Shaik, ..., S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan

item.title: [0★] Quantum-Chaos-Assisted Measure Synchronization in a Double-Well Ultracold Bose Gas
item.author: Xianchao Le, ..., Weiping Zhang, Keye Zhang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Xianchao Le, ..., Weiping Zhang, Keye Zhang

arXiv ID: 2611.27256 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

This paper investigates measure synchronization (MS) in a two-component ultracold atomic system confined in a double-well potential, which realizes a quantum many-body bosonic Josephson junction. Through spectral-statistics analysis, we identify the quantum chaotic parameter regime and confirm that the system achieves MS within this regime with weak dependence on the initial energy imbalance. We further show that chaotic dynamics not only significantly shortens the time scale for establishing synchronization but is also accompanied by entanglement entropy approaching the random-state prediction. These results reveal close connections among quantum chaos, MS, and quantum entanglement in conservative quantum many-body systems and may motivate further studies on the underlying mechanisms of chaos-assisted synchronization.

Xianchao Le, ..., Weiping Zhang, Keye Zhang

item.title: [0★] Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
item.author: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong

arXiv ID: 2611.27251 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to 4n4^n games on nn-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of LL pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with O(logL)O(\log L) classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. Our proof of the impossibility for memoryless channels relies on Stinespring's dilation theorem, while the impossibility for finite-memory channels relies on the optimal universal-NOT (in)fidelity bound by Bužek, Hillery, and Werner.

Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong

item.title: [0★] Unconventional Photon Blockade in Second-Order Nonlinearity Coupled Cavities with Asymmetric Dissipation
item.author: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, ..., Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, ..., Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou

arXiv ID: 2611.27200 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate the unconventional photon blockade in a second-order nonlinearity coupled double-cavity system with asymmetric dissipation. By treating the cavity decay rates as independent parameters, we analytically derive two exact families of optimal blockade conditions. While the first family recovers and generalizes the symmetric-dissipation results of previous studies, the second family, arising uniquely from an asymmetric dissipation ratio of κB=2κA\kappa_B = 2\kappa_A, completely locks the relative phase of the interference pathways. Importantly, we find that this asymmetric dissipation not only renders the optimal blockade condition strictly immune to frequency detuning, but also enhances the blockade depth by an order of magnitude compared to the resonant case. Furthermore, the mean photon number remains almost unaffected, proving that this enhanced robustness is achieved without sacrificing the brightness of the single-photon source. These findings offer a promising route toward robust single-photon generation in passive cavities with second-order nonlinearity.

Zhi-Qiang Zhang, ..., Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou

item.title: [0★] Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
item.author: Leonardo Gaytan, ..., Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Leonardo Gaytan, ..., Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh

arXiv ID: 2611.27140 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operating points. These results demonstrate a ``compute-in-place'' platform, with a logic and power footprint suited to future cryo-CMOS integration, that provides autonomous stabilization of quantum dots at desired operating points, creating an auto-tuning system for spin qubits that is resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations.

Leonardo Gaytan, ..., Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh

item.title: [0★] Generalized Wigner-Yanase Uncertainty Bounds for Multiple Quantum Channels
item.author: Jianming Zhou, Xiaoli Hu, Naihuan Jing
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Jianming Zhou, Xiaoli Hu, Naihuan Jing

arXiv ID: 2611.27034 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We derive uncertainty relations for quantum channels based on the generalized Wigner-Yanase skew information. For three channels, we obtain a product lower bound by optimizing over permutations of commutator and anticommutator pairings. For an arbitrary number of channels, we establish a lower bound on the sum of squared uncertainties and construct a hierarchy of bounds using the partial Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. These bounds are invariant under changes of Kraus representation for a fixed operator basis. The first two levels of the hierarchy coincide with the elementary arithmetic-geometric mean bound, while the intermediate levels generally depend on the ordering of the operator basis. Examples involving three and four qubit channels demonstrate the bounds and compare their performance with an earlier pairing inequality under fixed channel representations.

Jianming Zhou, Xiaoli Hu, Naihuan Jing

item.title: [0★] Augmenting Quantum Neural Networks with Contractive Layers
item.author: Bolin Huang, Pengfei Zhang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Bolin Huang, Pengfei Zhang

arXiv ID: 2611.27019 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Classical neural networks combine diverse layers with complementary roles to achieve rich expressive capabilities across complex learning tasks. Rapid advances in quantum science and technology have motivated growing interest in their quantum counterparts, quantum neural networks, raising the question of how their expressivity can be enhanced through the design of new quantum layers. Of particular interest are layers that enrich the accessible function space while introducing only a small number of additional trainable parameters. In this Letter, we introduce the contractive layer as a promising building block for quantum neural networks. This layer comprises all-to-all couplings governed by a single trainable parameter, enabling efficient control of quantum information flow while maintaining experimental relevance to Rydberg atom arrays. Using observable learning as a benchmark, we show that contractive layers enhance expressivity more efficiently than simply increasing the depth of conventional brick-wall circuits. This advantage stems from a systematic increase in the accessible target-space dimension per trainable parameter. We further demonstrate similar improvements in image recognition tasks. These results highlight contractive layers as a practical route to expressive quantum neural networks on near-term quantum devices.

Bolin Huang, Pengfei Zhang

item.title: [0★] Resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in one-dimensional quantum scattering
item.author: Víctor M. Villalba
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Víctor M. Villalba

arXiv ID: 2611.26960 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We study resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in a one-dimensional quantum-scattering model. Two incoming electrons scatter independently from a symmetric double-barrier structure and the sector with one reflected and one transmitted electron is selected. The idealised delta-function barriers used in earlier work are replaced by exponentially localised cusp barriers, U(x)=U0exp(−|x∓d/2|/a)U(x)=U_0\exp(-|x\mp d/2|/a), for which the single-barrier scattering problem is exactly solvable in terms of modified Bessel functions of imaginary order. We derive the corresponding reflection and transmission amplitudes, verify their current normalisation and validate them independently by direct numerical integration. Two separated cusp barriers are then combined through a Fabry-Pérot composition, whose accuracy is quantified by solving the full two-centre Schrödinger equation. In the well-separated regime the approximation reproduces the full resonance positions to high accuracy. The concurrence zeros are controlled by the resonance phase condition δ(κ)+κd=nπ\delta(\kappa)+\kappa d=n\pi, with a continuously unwrapped single-barrier reflection phase δ\delta. We also calculate the post-selection probability PRTP_{RT}, showing explicitly that large conditional concurrence can occur in a low-probability sector. Systematic scans in barrier width, integrated strength and reference momentum show that finite width can shift off-resonant concurrence maxima and, depending on the reference momentum, reduce their attainable height. The results identify resonance-controlled conditional entanglement as a robust feature of the well-separated double-barrier geometry rather than an artefact of the zero-range idealisation.

Víctor M. Villalba

item.title: [0★] Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
item.author: Jerry Horgan, ..., Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Jerry Horgan, ..., Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper

arXiv ID: 2611.26925 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.

Jerry Horgan, ..., Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper

item.title: [0★] Analog Explorations of Quantum State Measurement
item.author: Benjamin Krawciw, James P. Crutchfield
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Benjamin Krawciw, James P. Crutchfield

arXiv ID: 2611.26889 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The awkward disconnect in the postulates of quantum mechanics between the continuous, deterministic, linear, and unitary evolution governed by Schrödinger's equation and the discontinuous, stochastic, nonlinear, and nonunitary measurement process has vexed physicists for decades. Intuition from classical mechanics, statistical mechanics, and dynamical systems theory suggests that such a process might be modeled with a nonlinear system of differential equations. We explore such approaches by designing a deterministic model of an ideal projective measurement on a single qubit and constructing an analog computer that simulates it by manipulating voltages in an electrical circuit. The model reduces to Schrödinger evolution when no measurement is taking place. During a measurement, a hidden variable that the observer does not resolve selects the outcome, and the model is constructed so that a uniformly distributed hidden variable yields Born-rule frequencies. We do not derive the Born rule; rather, we show that a deterministic dynamical system with no intrinsic noise can implement it. Over 300 trials, the circuit reproduces the ideal model's individual outcomes to within one percent of the decision threshold, and its outcome frequencies match the Born rule to within about 0.02 in probability. These results are a small but provocative step towards modeling quantum measurement with macro-scale machines---a step of interest for both the foundations of physics and the alternatives to digital computing it suggests.

Benjamin Krawciw, James P. Crutchfield

item.title: [0★] Frequency-bin-encoded quantum secret sharing with fast basis switching
item.author: Chen-You Su, ..., Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Chen-You Su, ..., Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens

arXiv ID: 2611.26816 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Frequency-bin encoding offers unique opportunities for fiber-native quantum information processing, yet its full potential has been hampered by challenges in rapid state control and protocol scaling. Leveraging high-speed microwave processing, we overcome several extant hurdles and unlock new fundamental capabilities in frequency-based quantum communications. First, we demonstrate three-party quantum secret sharing, representing, to our knowledge, the first multiparty (N≥3N\geq 3 users) quantum communication protocol implemented entirely with frequency encoding. Second, we demonstrate active, pseudorandom switching of frequency-bin quantum states and measurement bases at 20 MHz symbol rates, enabling real-time protocol operation without relying on hardware-intensive passive basis-selection schemes. Even under fast switching, we preserve high-contrast three-party correlations (≥0.91\geq 0.91) and low quantum bit error rates (≤4.5%\leq 4.5\%). Our work extends frequency-bin quantum communication beyond static, two-party protocols, opening a pathway toward scalable, reconfigurable, and real-time spectrally encoded quantum networking.

Chen-You Su, ..., Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens

item.title: [0★] Gravity-induced entanglement assisted by an additional interaction using magic angle calibration
item.author: Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yanbei Chen
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yanbei Chen

arXiv ID: 2611.26755 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Gravity-induced entanglement provides an operational test of whether gravitational dynamics are compatible with local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but the weakness of the gravitational interaction and the presence of force noise make direct entanglement generation extremely demanding. We introduce a controllable additional coherent interaction that biases two test masses close to, but within, a separability-preservation bound, so that the weak Newtonian coupling supplies only the remaining coherent contribution needed for entanglement. If the additional interaction alone is shown to be incapable of generating entanglement, while entanglement is observed when gravity is included, the gravitational interaction provides a non-LOCC contribution. Since gravity cannot be turned off, we use a magic-angle null of the projected tidal coupling to calibrate the additional interaction and force noise. If the additional dynamics is certified to preserve separability at the magic angle and entanglement is subsequently observed in a non-null configuration, the gravitational contribution is incompatible with an LOCC description within the Markovian model. The protocol trades the stringent absolute force-noise requirement of direct schemes for precision in controlling the additional coupling, its backaction, and angle-dependent systematics.

Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yanbei Chen

item.title: [0★] Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
item.author: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

arXiv ID: 2611.26737 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

item.title: [0★] Cavity-Controlled Hysteresis and Multilevel Molecular Switching in Hybrid Optomechanics
item.author: Hugo Molinares, ..., Vitalie Eremeev, Eduardo Chamorro
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Hugo Molinares, ..., Vitalie Eremeev, Eduardo Chamorro

arXiv ID: 2611.26724 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate cavity-controlled hysteresis and multilevel molecular switching in a hybrid molecular optomechanical system composed of a plasmonic nanocavity, a Fabry-Pérot cavity, and an ensemble of molecular vibrations. Molecular-plasmonic optomechanical interaction together with cavity-plasmon hybridization produce bistability and dynamical hysteresis, leading to a history-dependent optical and molecular response. An analytical treatment of the steady-state equations shows that the auxiliary cavity renormalizes the effective optical linewidth and detuning, while the collective molecular interaction generates an effective nonlinearity. Together, these effects enable control of the hysteretic regime through optical detuning, cavity-plasmon coupling, and molecular ensemble size. Beyond bistability, pulsed excitation generates staircase-like molecular dynamics, with ascending or descending vibrational populations depending on the optical driving configuration. In particular, the FP cavity controls the buildup of vibrational excitation, while simultaneous driving of both optical modes enables stepwise vibrational depletion. These results establish hybrid molecular optomechanical systems as a tunable platform for history-dependent and pulse-driven molecular dynamics, with potential applications in nanoscale memory, multilevel information processing, and optically controlled molecular switching.

Hugo Molinares, ..., Vitalie Eremeev, Eduardo Chamorro

item.title: [0★] Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
item.author: Chen-Shen Lee, Itamar Kimchi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Chen-Shen Lee, Itamar Kimchi

arXiv ID: 2611.26693 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as PHP=0PHP=0, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.

Chen-Shen Lee, Itamar Kimchi

item.title: [0★] Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
item.author: Marco Vaia, ..., Matteo M. Wauters, Philipp Hauke

Authors: Marco Vaia, ..., Matteo M. Wauters, Philipp Hauke

arXiv ID: 2611.26695 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group D3D_3, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.

Marco Vaia, ..., Matteo M. Wauters, Philipp Hauke

item.title: [0★] Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
item.author: Alireza Maleki
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Alireza Maleki

arXiv ID: 2611.26659 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

Alireza Maleki
